metadata.pr_description: Introduce a unified serialization method for various data types, improving consistency and maintainability. Enhance Pinecone integration to utilize VectorStore and handle import errors gracefully. Add comprehensive tests for the new serialization functions.

review_planner.summary: The changes involve refactoring serialization logic across multiple files and introducing a new serialization module. The main changes include replacing the old `serialize_field` and `recursive_serialize_or_str` functions with a new `serialize` function from `langflow.serialization.serialization`. Additionally, there are updates to handle specific types like `Decimal` and `Document`, and the introduction of constants for maximum text and item lengths.

tasks.title: Security Review
tasks.description: Verify that the new serialization logic does not introduce any security vulnerabilities, especially around data truncation and handling of potentially malicious input. Check for any potential injection points or unsafe operations.

tasks.title: Logic Review
tasks.description: Verify the correctness of the new serialization logic in `serialize` function. Ensure that all types are handled correctly and that the logic for truncating strings and lists works as intended. Check the updated `build_vector_store` method in `pinecone.py` for correct handling of imports and exceptions.

tasks.title: Performance Review
tasks.description: Evaluate the performance impact of the new serialization logic. Check for any inefficiencies introduced by the new serialization function and ensure that the truncation logic does not cause unnecessary overhead. Also, verify that the new imports in `pinecone.py` do not introduce additional latency.

tasks.title: General Review
tasks.description: Review the overall changes for consistency and adherence to coding standards. Verify that the new serialization logic is well-documented and that the refactoring does not break existing functionality. Ensure that the new constants for maximum text and item lengths are used consistently across the codebase.
